column2: Arundhati among chaste women, Tilottama among the apsarases, and Chiti, the one named Brahmakala, the power of all embodied beings.
This excellent list of a hundred and eight names has been told by way of indication; a hundred and eight holy places are declared.
Whoever recites it on rising at dawn goes to the supreme goal. The men who bathe at these holy places and see these goddesses
are freed from all sins and go to the supreme goal. The man who gives up his body at Uma's abodes
pierces through Brahma's abode and reaches Shankara's state. Whoever recites the hundred and eight names in Shiva's presence
on the third and eighth days becomes a man with many sons; reciting it at the gift of a cow, at the time of shraddha, at a wedding and in auspicious rites,
or in the rite of worshipping the gods, one attains Brahma-hood. Having heard this incomparable hymn and bowed to the mountain,
the king, for the release of his ancestors and for the sake of a sacrifice, said to the Kalpaga: "At what holy place would a sacrifice give release to the ancestors?"
Having heard this, great king, and bowed to the Kalpaga, the king went to his city with Vasishtha and the others.
A lakh of cows with calves and ten thousand that had not yet calved, twenty of dark-eared horses and a hundred thousand horses,
adorned with gems, rubies, pearls and the like, radiant as Uchchaihshravas, and ten thousand lordly elephants shining with bells and ornaments —
the gems, rubies and jewels could not be counted — with kings of many lands and brahmins versed in the Veda,
with the sound of flutes and vinas and the roar of Vedic chanting, filling all the quarters and touching heaven and earth,
filled with great joy, furnished with the materials of sacrifice, King Rantideva came to the bank of the Kalpaga.
There the foods and eatables of many kinds were beyond number; for eight yojanas there were sacrificial posts and pavilions,
pillars of gold and jewels adorned with gems and pearls, golden fire-pits and altars by the thousand,
spoons and vessels of sacrifice all of gold. Then the gods were invited — Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara,
the moon and sun with the planets, the sphere of stars and the pole, siddhas, vidyadharas, yakshas, gods, asuras and great serpents,
the king of the gods and the gods headed by Brihaspati. Then the sacrifice was begun by brahmins versed in the Veda.
By the oblation the gods dwelling in all worlds were satisfied; the fire blazed smokeless with its seven tongues,
and the bearer of oblations himself was present in the sacrifice, lord of men. Then the sacrifice was completed by brahmins who received fees,
and a proclamation was carried through the kingdom by chamberlains by the thousand: "Whatever desire anyone desires, he shall have it here, without doubt."
The ancestors were invited there, of the mother's and the father's lines; those who had come under the sway of untimely death and those gone into animal births —
all attained auspicious births through the sacrifice. The goddess Narmada was worshipped, present in bodily form;
the blessed Hara was worshipped there together with Parvati, and the lord of Shri with Shri, bearing conch, discus and mace,
and the gods headed by Shakra with their wives, adorned. He gave cows, horses and lordly elephants to the brahmins,
and whatever else there was — wealth, grain, milk, curd, fire-cleansed garments — he gave it all to them.
The gods Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara were worshipped together; the goddess Narmada was worshipped, standing at the foot of the mountain,
where the stream came forth at the meeting of the Kubja and Reva. The ancestors and gods were satisfied and reached the supreme goal.
The best of kings, Dadhichi too, mounted a divine vehicle; a hundred and eight in front, and behind them after that,
the good by the hundreds on the path of the gods, best of kings. And all the gods headed by Brahma said to Rantideva:
Choose a boon — blessings on you — we are pleased by this truth, O king; you have reached the supreme world with your fathers and mothers.
Rantideva said: "If you are givers of boons to me — where the pot was set up by the brahmins versed in the Veda,
devotees bearing the four Vedas, let there be a Shiva linga there, whose very body is the five Brahmans, radiant with garlands of flame."
Reaching the mountain of sacrifice, a stream came forth from the sacrifice: from the bathing came forth the Kubja, from the charu the Charuka,
the Charmila at the foot, and from the craftwork the Shilpa. Kubera and the other gods, having worshipped and bowed,
and bowing to the Kalpaga, mounted vehicles that went at will. The creator of the world, lord of the worlds, fortunate one,
bowing according to rule, composed a hymn to the trident-bearer in linga form. Brahma said: "There is no god equal to Rudra, no guru equal to Rudra.
Salutation to you, lord of gods, whose body is ever pure, whose form is spotless with its own radiance, whose body-paste is Shiva's ash;
salutation to you, the blue-throated god, whose form is all-embracing and immeasurable, of many forms, lovely and eternal;
salutation to you, the supreme, the supreme Lord, the all-knowing, to whose body all bow and who yourself bow to none;
salutation to the three-eyed trident-bearer, worshipful even among the worshipful, known to Brahma, Indra and Vishnu, cause of origin and continuance;
praised by the gods, salutation to you, giver of enjoyment and liberation; to Vama, of lovely form, shining with lovely Uma beside you,
half of whose body is your lovely beloved — salutation to you, Ishana." Hearing this hymn of Brahma, the god of boundless splendour,
Shankara said: "Choose the boon you desire at the sacrifice; I will give it to you without doubt, whatever boon you wish."
Brahma spoke to Shankara, the all-pervading lord: "The five-faced one, the five lingas, declared worthy of Brahma's worship —
in which bilva fruits were offered and mangoes too were offered — let the linga named Bilvamraka, which carries across the ocean of worldly existence,
attain supreme renown by your grace, lord. Where the Vamana and Mekala are, where this excellent linga is,
bathing there, tiger among men, Shiva's world is attained. This I regard as the boon that brings grace to the worlds."
Shankara said "So be it" to the imperishable Brahma. Having said this, Maheshana, surrounded by crores of ganas,
praised by all the gods, went to his own abode, and the gods headed by Brahma went each to his own dwelling.
Rantideva praised Shiva bearing the form of the linga; hearing Rantideva's hymn, Maheshvara said:
Choose a boon — blessings on you — for this hymn, man of good vows. Rantideva said: "If Shiva is a giver of boons to me,
never abandon this holy place, Mahadeva. Those men flooded by masses of sin who have gone into animal births —
by the greatness of this holy place let them go to the supreme goal; whatever gift is given here, let it all be imperishable.
This I regard as the boon, if you are pleased, Shankara." Shankara said: "At the conjunction of the new moon with a Monday and on the full moon of Kartika,
whatever gift is given here obtains endless fruit." This I have told you, O king, the holy place that destroys sin.
The Vishvedevas attained supreme perfection at this holy place; Agastya, Shaunaka, Parashara and Aghamarshana
and hosts of other sages attained supreme perfection; here ten thousand sages rose to heaven by austerity.
At the solar transit, at vyatipata, at eclipses of moon and sun, at the conjunction of the new moon with a Monday and at the Shadashitimukha,
merit increases tenfold — this truth was spoken by Shiva. A crore and a quarter of holy places are at the meeting of the Kubja and Reva,
established within a krosha on the southern and northern sides. Whoever gives up his life there, helplessly or willingly,
becomes a king in the city of the vidyadharas for thousands of years. Worms, insects, moths and the like, on giving up life at this holy place,
become kings in the city of the vidyadharas for a thousand divine years. Bilvamraka is a Siddhalinga giving the fruits of desire and enjoyment;
and another great one, Kubjeshvara, removes the sin of killing a brahmin. In this stretch, great king, the wise know Shiva's field.
At the meeting of the Reva and Kubja, seventy barley-grains' breadth; at the conjunction of the new moon with a Monday, peace is declared from bathing.
Varanasi, Kurukshetra, Prayaga, Naimisha, Pushkara, Gaya and the excellent holy place Kedara —
at these the fruit at the conjunction of the new moon with a Monday is ordinary; at the meeting of the Kubja and Reva the fruit is declared imperishable.
By giving sesame water a son may raise from hell all his mother's and father's lines, both those before and those after.
That king too reached home, having raised all his forebears. This I have told you, O king, of the meeting of the Kubja and Reva.
Rantideva, Harishchandra, Puruhuta and Pururavas, having sacrificed here with many kinds of sacrifices, shine in heaven like gods.
By hearing and reciting of this holy place, best of men, one's self is purified of all sins and one is honoured in Shiva's world.
Renowned as Suvarnadvipa, surrounded by the divine valley — Harita, Gautama, Vishnu, Savarni and Kaushika,
these and many other sages of praised vows; some fasting for a month, others fasting for a fortnight,
others devoted to the chandrayana, others practising the krichchhra; some living on fruits and roots, others living on air,
others drinking the smoke of grain, others living on water; some standing on one foot, others standing on half a foot,
some using their teeth as a mortar, others gazing at the sun; and brahmins who know Brahman, skilled in Shruti and Smriti,
reflecting on the Itihasas and Puranas and the means of liberation, ever devoted to the agnihotra, devoted to japa, sacrifice and rites —
with the resounding of Vedic recitation they carry the three worlds across. Sin cannot move there, as darkness at sunrise.
On the southern bank of the Mekala it stands like Brahma's world, with mango, jambu, kadamba, kapittha, bilva and pomegranate,
banana, citron and the like, jambira and jackfruit, adorned with many trees, chief among them banyan and badari,
with punnaga, nagabakula, ashoka and tilaka, mandara, champaka, amrataka, blue lotuses and lotuses,
adorned with all trees furnished with leaves, flowers and fruits, with many hosts of birds, frequented by siddhas and gandharvas.
All the birds speak with the speech of men, O king; endowed with these qualities is the excellent Suvarnadvipa.
In the Svayambhuva Manvantara, O king, in the first kalpa, in the Krita age, by worshipping the god of gods, the dwellers of Suvarnadvipa,
casting off all darkness, sport in Shankara's world. By the gift of food to the ancestors and the gift of sesame water,
having removed their impurity, they dwell in Brahma's city. On the holy full moon of Kartika, O king, it grants the fruit of all holy places.
Men in the Kali age, deluded by maya, do not see this. On the southern side of the Kalpaga are crores of holy places in many ways;
it is renowned among perfected sages and known only to them. By unbelievers who have broken the bounds, revilers of the Puranas and Smritis,
anointed with oil, not doing what the Veda enjoins on the bank of the Reva, deluded by the maya of Kali, that place is not seen.
At the place of Hiranyagarbha, where the Kalpaga flows, the Shiva linga named Yajnagarbheshvara is proclaimed,
worshipped by siddhas, gandharvas, gods, asuras and great serpents, where King Vaivasvata, the greatly famous son of the Sun,
by the greatness of that holy place became moon-faced. In the month of Chaitra, in the bright fortnight, lord of men,
on the fourteenth and the full moon, when Hara is present there, by giving sesame water and pindas, O Bharata,
one who gives abundant fees raises the ancestors from hell there and dwells in Vishnu's world as long as the moon and sun are seen.
Whatever gift is given there equals Kurukshetra; those who give up life there do not see Yama's abode.
On the northern bank of the Reva is the mountain named Paryanka, a glorious son of the Vindhya, made of all gods, auspicious.
There Keshava himself stands as Vishnu the remover of sin, remover of men's sin, resting on the bank of the Narmada.
Bathing there, great king, one gains the fruit of a thousand cows; his ancestors, satisfied, go content to Hari's city.
The man who observes the eleventh or twelfth day there has no return to the hard-to-bear mortal world.
Hari's field is declared to be a krosha in extent; those who died by untimely death go to the supreme goal.
The brahmins fallen by a curse were released there by Narada; by the greatness of that holy place the gods rejoice in heaven.
With flowers and fruits of many trees, endowed with every desire, frequented by many hosts of birds, served by many trees,
by siddhas, vidyadharas, yakshas, gandharvas and kinnaras, with the sound of flutes and vinas and the noise of conches and instruments,
the meeting of the Narmada and the Vindhya always shines, O king, where the gods headed by Brahma and Shakra are free of sorrow.
That is the hermitage of the Vishvedevas, saluted by all gods; the sons of Vishva are proclaimed as the Vishvedevas,
and Kashyapa begot them in the Ashoka grove, when the Vaivasvata Manvantara had come, in the Treta age, best of men.
Fifty thousand auspicious holy places dwell there; there Savitri was perfected, and Aditi, mother of the gods,
Devayani, Indrani, Rohini, Sambharayani, Dakshayani honoured by the world, Lopamudra of great fame,
Ratnavali wife of the Sun, Dhruva, Tara and Ganeshvari; the ashokas planted by him stand there, a hundred in number.
By the greatness of this holy place a man is freed from sin. On the fourteenth of the bright fortnight in the month of Ashvina, O Bharata,
a woman without sons, barren, unlucky or without a husband, bathed with the five gems and fruits, should worship with divine pots;
for a thousand births she becomes again blessed with sons and fortune. In the field of the Ashoka grove a boon was granted there by Gauri,
where the goddess Narmada flows through seven kalpas. There Dharmaraja and the great-souled Varuna sacrificed,
and Nairritya and the other world-guardians according to rule; the bearer of oblations came in person to the world-guardians.
Atri, Marichi and Kashyapa performed an excellent sacrifice there; giving and other rites there are a hundred times greater than in another field.
Varanasi, Kurukshetra, Gaya and Naimisha, Mayapuri, Pushkara, Prayaga and the moon-crested one,
the Kashyapi — all holy places are where the Kalpaga abides; they know no other holy place equal to the Ashoka grove.
There long ago the horse sacrifice, the best of rites, was performed, O king; there Brahma long ago released brahmins from the birth of dogs,
dwellers of Pataliputra, by the greatness of this holy place. Yudhishthira said: How, dear one, did the Self-born perform the horse sacrifice?
And how were the brahmins formerly released from the birth of dogs? And who, O brahmin, was the king of old who was equal to the king of the gods?
Tell me all this properly, best of sages. Markandeya said: Listen, fortunate king, to an ancient account.
Greatly deluded men, bewildered by sin, do not know the holy place of the Ashoka grove on the bank of the Kalpaga,
a holy place more secret than the secret, the very best of all holy places; the Vishokeshvara linga there gives supreme success;
it is worshipped by siddhas and gandharvas; men do not see it. By seeing and touching it one removes the sin of killing a brahmin.
When the Svayambhuva Manvantara had come, in the first kalpa, in the Krita age, Ravichandra, great king, a greatly famous emperor,
born in the lunar line, lord of Kanchipura, ruled the whole earth as Shakra rules heaven.
The lord of the earth went to a place crowded with many trees, frequented by many hosts of birds and served by many sages,
where there is the auspicious shrine of Shambhu named Agastyeshvara, served by all the ascetic sages headed by Agastya.
At the conjunction of Rahu and the sun, Ravichandra, best of kings, where the Kalpaga of seven kalpas flows and the mountain Amarakantaka is,
with elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers, with treasury, army and vehicles, came to the great-souled one practising austerity, surrounded by throngs of sages,
Maitravaruni, blazing like fire. Rising from among them, Shandilya, of great austerity,
prostrating himself on the ground, asked Agasti: "Ravichandra of great radiance has come to your hermitage;
know that I am his priest, treasury of austerity; he longs to worship your feet, if you deem it a favour."
Agastya said: "Let the best of kings come quickly." Seated on his throne, the king came with his permission and clasped his feet,
and having honoured him with arghya and foot-water the sage asked how he fared: "Are you well, fortunate one, with your women and retinue?"
The king spoke to the lord of sages, O Bharata: "Today my birth, my kingdom and my life are fruitful,
and I am freed from sin by the sight of your lotus feet. The Kalpaga is holy everywhere, auspicious and made of all holy places.
In what place shall I perform a sacrifice? Tell me, best of sages, so that the sacrifice may be accomplished and the gods' satisfaction be imperishable.
Tell me all this properly, knower of the three times." Agastya said: "Listen, fortunate king, and understand what I tell you.
It was told long ago by Shiva to Parvati and Shanmukha, to Brahma, Vishnu and the other gods and to the other dwellers in heaven.
I heard it there, O king, together with the long-lived Markandeya; I shall tell you that which arises from the holy places of the Mekala.
Listen, all you sages, to the descent that is to be asked about. Who has the power, great king, except Maheshvara,
to give the measure or number of all the holy places from the beginning? I merely indicate what the great sage Markandeya told."
This I have told you, O king, as it happened long ago.
Neither the Sarasvati nor the Ganga nor the Yamuna nor the oceans, nor other holy places headed by Prayaga —
the Narmada alone is holy, auspicious, flowing through seven kalpas. Jambudvipa is declared to be a lakh of yojanas in extent;
by drinking the water of the Narmada, in Lokaloka with the moving and unmoving, even men without austerity go to Shiva's abode.
Whatever desire one desires, he obtains it abundantly. Well done, well done, fortunate one, that you have asked me, sinless one.
To whom would the divine and delightful Narmada, when told of, not be pleasing? As many holy places as there are on the southern and northern banks,
so many that give you delight I shall tell, best of kings; others I cannot recount even in a lakh of verses.
The three Vedas, the three worlds, the three twilights, the three fires, siddhas, gandharvas, yakshas with kinnaras and great serpents,
vidyadharas and apsarases rest on the bank of the Kalpaga; the lingas beginning with Omkara and the mountains beginning with Vaidurya of old,
in the Dvapara and on reaching the Kali, attained purifying power. Now the bounds of the gods Brahma, Vishnu and the rest are told.
South and north of the Reva shining with radiance, this is renowned as the ground of sacrifice, saluted by gods and asuras.
The Ashoka grove is there, and its god is Maheshvara; there the sacrifice is accomplished without obstacle, so said Shankara."
The king spoke to Agastya, best of sages: "Blessings on you; I shall go with you, great sage."
The king, surrounded by sages, reached the Ashoka grove, on the southern bank of the Reva, among splendid holy places.
For ten yojanas there were sacrificial posts and a pavilion, adorned at all the doors with masses of gems, rubies and jewels,
rich with the splendour of banners and flags, covered with many cloths. Vishvamitra, Bharadvaja, Kashyapa and Bhargava,
Brahmadrishya, Lomasha and other best of sages, the most fortunate Valakhilyas, the mind-born sons of Brahma —
these and many other sages of praised vows. Then the sacrifice was carried on by brahmins who received fees.
All the gods, satisfied, returned to heaven, and all the sages, delighted, went to their own hermitages.
Then, when the sacrifice was completed, Durvasas went away angry: "Neither Vaivasvata nor I nor Narada nor Parvata were here;
how was the sacrifice completed by sinful, vile men?" Yama came there, and Narada and Parvata,
the scribe Chitragupta, Kala and Mrityu likewise; all these were angry at being without a share of the sacrifice, O king.
Seeing them all angry, Ravichandra said: "By the grace of the god Ashokeshvara and of the Narmada,
who among the hosts of gods and asuras is able to obstruct me? And likewise, who else among creatures could be a cause of obstruction to the sacrifice?
Whatever man has come at the time of sacrifice is to be honoured and worshipped like the four-armed god.
As you have come, fortunate and mighty sons of Brahma, I will give you whatever you desire in your minds, without doubt."
Durvasas said: "Our son Narada and Parvata are to be honoured; I do not ask alone; we ask together."
Ravichandra said: "Whatever desire anyone desires, I give it to him." Thus all those eminent sages were addressed by him,
and made well pleased by the giving of arghya and foot-water, O king. Yudhishthira said: For what reason were the sages dwelling in Pataliputra
cursed by the Goddess into the birth of dogs, and how were they freed? Markandeya said: Long ago all the ascetics, wearing matted locks and bark,
in Nepal worshipped Pashupati, the god of gods Maheshvara, Shiva, with devotion — Hara without Gauri,
not the god Ardhanarishvara, saluted by gods and asuras; for that deed, as splitters of the linga, they were cursed by Parvati:
For a thousand years you will go into the birth of dogs, sinners who eat the old offerings, eaters of what belongs to Chanda.
On their behalf, great king, Durvasas said to the king: "Those lords of sages have gone into the birth of dogs at that time;
release them, O king, wishing to do what pleases us; cursed by Parvati, they are sinking in dreadful hell."
The king said to the sage Durvasas: "I will release those excellent brahmins from that sin, without doubt."
He sent servants to the forest where they were languishing; bowing, they all spoke to those forest-dwellers,
reminding them of their former birth, as instructed by their master. Then at their word they quickly came to the Ashoka grove.
The emperor Ravichandra, seeing those ascetics, filled with supreme joy, spoke to them as if smiling:

By the power of the god Ashokeshvara and of the Mekala, by the power of my gifts and the grace of the great sages,
skandapuran:66:41	let the sages leave the birth of dogs and go to Shiva's world; let all this most dreadful sin settle on me.
At that moment, freed from the curse, they mounted vehicles that went at will; the great sages said to Ravichandra, a Shatakratu:
You are our mother, you our father, our guru, giver of liberation. Having said this, they went to the supreme city of Uma and Maheshvara.

Well done, well done, fortunate one; you are a treasury of sacrifice and austerity; there is no other king in the lunar line equal to you;
skandapuran:66:45	by you the three worlds with the moving and unmoving have been won. Having said this, the best of gods honoured him with praise.
The drums of the gods sounded and a rain of flowers fell. Durvasas said: "Among kshatriyas I have neither seen nor heard of one equal to you.
Giving up life is easy; giving up dharma is hard. Choose a boon — blessings on you — whatever is in your mind."
The king said with a smile to the sage Durvasas: "By the power of my gifts, let men of evil minds
attain the supreme world — this is the boon dear to me." Saying "So be it" before him, the eminent sage,
filled with supreme joy, vanished right there. Seeing such a deed of the king of boundless radiance,
Dharmaraja, filled with great apprehension, said this: "I give you a boon — blessings on you — though excluded from the share of the sacrifice.
Brahmins gone into the birth of dogs have been released from the bonds of karma; such is your power, I know, best of kings.
A deed hard on earth, and sacrifice especially — whoever gives away his own excellent merit, fortunate one,
has won Yama's world and the world of the gods; you are worthy of a boon, king of kings — this truth I have spoken."
Ravichandra said: "If you are pleased, son of the Sun, and wish to give me a boon — by my hundred sacrifices, by my gifts and austerity,
let those in sinful births and those who do evil go, by your grace, Dharmaraja, to Shiva's abode.
This I regard as the boon; show me this favour." Yama said: "So be it, king of kings, devoted to truth and dharma;
attain the supreme world by this truth, man of good vows, since all those of sinful birth have been released from their impurity by you.
Kshatriyas by the hundreds, O king, and others by the thousands raised from sin — their number cannot be counted."
Having said this to the best of kings, mighty-armed Dharmaraja mounted a vehicle that went at will, saluted by gods and asuras,
and went to his own abode, O king, and Narada and Parvata too. In it, best of men, eighty lakhs of holy places
in the Ashoka grove have been declared to you, sinless one; by hearing and reciting them one gains the fruit of a thousand cows.
Thus King Brahmadatta, best of all kings, furnished with all materials, carried on the sacrifice,
with the resounding of Vedic recitation and the sound of song and music, praised by hosts of Maruts mounted on many vehicles.
By Brahmadatta's sacrifice, by the grace of Vagisha and the grace of the Narmada, the pretas attained supreme satisfaction.
Yudhishthira said: How did Brahmadatta sacrifice on the bank of the Kalpaga? How were the pretas released, and by what deed had they become pretas?
Tell me all this properly, rich in austerity. Markandeya said: Listen, O king, to an ancient history, as is fitting.
On reaching the festival of the full moon of Kartika at Pushkara, at Jyeshthapushkara, Ayogandha, Svayambhu and Pundarikaksha,
the Grandsire himself, teacher and father of gods and asuras, Kavya and Hotrisadana, Vedagarbha, Kritadhvana,
Svastika, Savitra, Vamadeva and Aghamarshana — these and other sages, born of a portion of Brahma's radiance —
they, according to their ability, approached their wives in season; established in household life, their wives were devoted to serving their husbands,
wearing rags and bark, eating vegetables and wild millet; dejected by that dharma, even those truthful women reproached them:

The six duties of a brahmin are sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, teaching, study, giving and receiving gifts;
skandapuran:67:25	ornaments and clothing and service to the husband belong to women. Thus the husbands were reproached by the women, O king,
and they were all afraid, astonished and downcast. "King Harishchandra of old — there has been none like him nor will be,
by whose giving the three worlds with moving and unmoving were won; he went to Kurukshetra at the conjunction of Rahu and the sun."
Leaving the holy place Pushkara, deluded by greed for wealth, the sages, a thousand in number, with their wives and sons,
went where King Harishchandra was, eager to receive gifts. Harishchandra, filled with supreme joy, said to the sages:
Blessed and fruitful is my pilgrimage to Kurukshetra at the eclipse of the sun — tormented by hunger and suffering, children and elders thin and afflicted,
wearing bark and deerskin, like ghosts in their youth — "since you have come to us with your wives and sons."
The king spoke, prostrating with eight limbs: "Give me your command; what shall I do for you?"
Having said this, the glorious one gave to each separately a lakh of gold and cows by the thousand,
a thousand horses and a hundred elephants, lovely seven-storeyed houses with golden walls and arches,
and pleasures of many kinds, as if he were the lord of wealth himself. Dying in another kalpa, they were born in the form of pretas, terrifying,
with hanging lips and hanging testicles, with deformed faces; by the power of receiving gifts a brahmin's fall is certain.
Remembering their births, they grieved for themselves, alone outside: "No wife, no sons, no servants, no kin of mine —
they were not burned by the gifts as we were; we alone are burned, like trees by fire.
Men burned by gifts from kings do not sprout again; for those burned by fire there is rebirth.
Neither mother nor father nor son nor wealth nor kin — for those seized by Yama's messengers dharma alone is the companion."
Having grieved a long time, without wives and sons, having wandered the whole earth, they came to the holy place Pushkara.
Seeing the sages in the form of pretas, the best of sages fell into the greatest sorrow and said to them: "How have you become pretas?"
The pretas said: "Harishchandra, true to dharma, king in the solar line, the glorious lord of Ayodhya, valorous as a god —
we received gifts from him when the sun was in eclipse; by that all we brahmin sages became pretas, O sage.
This we have told you, O brahmin; let our release be arranged." The son of Brahma, knower of the truth of future and past, treasury of austerity,
the glorious Narada, said to those ascetics: "On a holy occasion, on the divine festival of the full moon of Kartika,
it was told by Shiva long ago to Parvati and Shanmukha; I too heard there the Purana proclaimed by Skanda.
What other river can destroy sin except the Reva, O king? The Ganga and other rivers, brahmins, and holy places too —
and the city of Vagisha there, resting on the bank of the Narmada: at Brahmadatta's sacrifice there will be release."
Having given the direction, Narada went to heaven. And those pretas, fortunate one, meditating on Shiva, husband of Uma,
went to that region, the excellent city of Vagisha; bathing there and worshipping Shiva, Hari and the sun,
at Brahmadatta's sacrifice they were all freed from sin; mounting Brahma's vehicle they came to Brahma's world,
shining like suns, bearing bodies of Brahma's radiance; a rain of flowers fell upon the king.
This I have told you, O king, as it happened long ago; by hearing and reciting it one gains the fruit of a thousand cows.
Fruitful are Vedic sacrifices and pilgrimage to holy places, O Bharata; yet men intent on receiving gifts torment themselves.
The giver and the beggar are indicated by their very hands: the receiver goes down and the giver goes up.
The holy place named Sahasravartaka destroys sin; for one who bathes there according to rule there is the fruit of releasing a bull;
it purifies seven generations of one's family, no doubt. On the northern bank of the Reva, a thousand weapons in number,
and at its end, fortunate one, is the excellent forest of Kara, where one gains the fruit of the agnishtoma and, having bathed, goes to heaven.
On the northern side of the Reva is a most splendid holy place, the forest named Saugandhika; celibates of pure vows,
the ancestors, Brahma and the other great ascetics, siddhas, charanas, gandharvas, kinnaras and great serpents sprinkled it;
entering that forest a mortal is freed from all sin. Then there is the Sarasvati, best of rivers,
Lakshya, daughter of the gods, O king, declared most holy; a man should bathe in its water, O king,
and having satisfied the ancestors and gods gains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. The holy place named Ishanadhyushita there is very rare;
bathing there at vyatipata, the solar transit or an eclipse, a man gains the fruit of giving a thousand tawny cows and of a horse sacrifice.
Going to Sugandha, Shatakumbha and the Five Sacrifices, O Bharata, best of men, one is honoured in the world of heaven.
Reaching right there the holy place called Trishula, O Bharata, whoever bathes there and worships the ancestors and gods
attains lordship of the ganas on leaving the body, no doubt. Then one should go, great king, to the unsurpassed Brahmasthana,
on the northern bank of the Reva, giving the fruit of desires and enjoyments, renowned as Brahmoda, conspicuous on earth, O Bharata.
There the seven sages came to bathe, bull of the Bharatas; Kapinjala, best of sages, Havyavaha, O Bharata,
the blessed Devayana and the great sage Vishvavasu attained Brahma's world by the greatness of this holy place.
By the gift of shraddha the ancestors went to Brahma's city. Having duly beheld the udumbara,
one attains invisibility, one's sin burned away by austerity. Then one should go, great king, to Shankara, who brings good to the world.
Going to the bull-bannered one on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, one obtains all desires and goes to the world of heaven.
On the southern side of the Narmada is a great Siddhalinga of gems, more secret than the secret, which men do not see;
it is worshipped by the lords of serpents, gods, siddhas and naga maidens; a crore and a quarter of holy places are at Shankara, delight of the Kurus.
The holy hermitage of the Vasus, of celibate sages devoted to Shiva, living on bulbs, roots and fruits —
by giving sesame water there the ancestors' satisfaction is imperishable; the giver, filled with supreme joy, goes to Shiva's abode.
Dhruva, Dhara, Soma, Savitra, Anala, Anila, Pratyusha and Prabhasa are declared the eight Vasus;
by Shankara's grace they attained divinity in heaven. On the northern side of the Kalpaga is the unsurpassed Somatirtha;
bathing there, O king, a man is honoured in the world of heaven. Then one should go, best of kings, to the holy place Saptasarasvata.
Hear the hymn made by Brahma, you of holy fame. Brahma said: "May Vasudeva, the lord of speech, ever be my refuge.
The swan, lord of gods, the speaker, dwelling within the Vasus, the priest, lord of the dwellers in heaven — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Svaha, Svadha and Vashat, eater of oblations, embodiment of the Rik, embodiment of the Yajus — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The supreme knower of the field, subtle, Hari who carries the worlds across, the Lord dwelling in the heart — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Worthy to be heard, the means of hearing, of holy fame, of pure renown, giver of boons, Vasudeva who is fire — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The Person, lotus-eyed, ancient, lord of the worlds, the fire within the sun — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Slayer of Kamsa and Kaliya, mighty, crusher of Bala, the fire that slew Shishupala — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The fire that slew Kalanemi, the appointed ender in time, destroyer of the bodies of a hundred asuras — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Slayer of the asura Kanka, destroyer of Madhu and Kaitabha, with conch, discus and mace in hand — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The white one lying on the waters, Vishnu, called the destroyer of sin, Indra, true keeper of his word — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Hrishikesha, protector of Indra, Upendra, seated on Garuda, of a thousand names, knower of dharma — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Bearer of conch, Nandaka and discus, Sharnga-bowed, mace-bearing, steadfast, embodied, wise — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The great Sankarshana, Shambhu, self-born, sustainer of beings, skilful, marked, pure — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Of the three times, knower of the three times, maker of the three Vedas, three-eyed, of the three Samans, son of Devaki — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Of unmanifest self, great-souled, the inner self, Janardana, breath, self of the senses and elements — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The supreme self, supreme Brahman, supreme lord, supreme goal, the Supreme, the supreme light — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
Self of the universe, maker of the universe, lord of the universe, self-possessed, maker of heaven and earth — may Vasudeva be my refuge.
The Lord thousand-headed, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, bearing thousands of crores — may Vasudeva be my refuge."
Thus the eloquent lord of speech worshipped the supreme Lord. May the blessed Vishnu, Janardana, be pleased with me, his devotee.
Whatever merit I have earned since birth, may its whole fruit be eternal, supreme Person.
For one who constantly practises this, Keshava is worshipped; it destroys sins and reveals its fruit.
This is the thornless path, where Hari is worshipped; one should know that as the wrong path where Hari is not worshipped.
The Vedas are devoted to Vasudeva, rites are devoted to Vasudeva, brahmins are of Vasudeva's nature, the refuge is devoted to Vasudeva.
All the gods worship Vasudeva, all the gods were born of Vasudeva; Vasudeva is the god of all; there is nothing other, nothing beyond Vasudeva.
There is no god holier, no austerity beyond Vishnu, no knowledge beyond Vishnu; the whole world is made of Vishnu.
Men who recite with devotion this hymn marked with Vishnu's names go to Vishnu's world, the supreme eternal Brahman.
